state-dependent: the same parameters returned err=1 in an isolated probe where the arm started at tx=+208. Mate-flag outcome depends on the pre-mate pose, so flag search is not a reliable closure path.

established: The arm CAN be mated by reference planes: the pairing is arm.front <-> sc.right at 0 deg with a 208.0 mm offset, plus a 25 deg arm.top <-> sc.top clock angle.
PARALLEL and COINCIDENT mates on these planes succeed with zero drift.

The 208 mm DISTANCE mate is the single unresolved element: its direction/orientation outcome depends on alignment+flip AND on the pre-mate pose, and no tested combination gave err=1 with BOTH zero translation and zero rotation drift in the production sequence.
conclusion.next_method: Stop searching mate flags. Apply the mate set, then explicitly restore the G0-frozen component transform via the verified VARIANT CreateTransform + SetTransformAndSolve3 primitive, then re-verify PRE/POST drift <= 0.01 mm / 0.01 deg and that mates report no errors. This makes the mate carry design intent while the frozen transform remains the numerical authority.
